Rahul Singh Chouhan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5
February, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:10380

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice B. P. Sharma

On The 5 th Of February, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 57681 of 2025
 Rahul Singh Chouhan
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Hakim Khan Qureshi - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Ms. Papiya Ghosh - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State
 Order

The present petition under Section 528 of BNSS, 2023 has been filed by the petitioner challenging the issuance of arrest warrants and the orders passed by learned Trial Court rejecting the petitioner's applications for cancellation of warrants in RCT No.7129/2020, RCT No.7128/2020 and RCT No.8066/2020 and seeking a direction to learned Trial Court to consider the petitioner's application under Section 70(2) of CrPC, 1973 (Section 72(2) of the BNSS, 2023) in light of the subsequent compliance of the bail conditions.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that Crime No.266/2020, Crime No.267/2020 and Crime No.398/2020 were registered against the petitioner at Police Station Ayodhya Nagar, Bhopal (M.P.) for offences punishable under Sections 420, 406 and 120-B of IPC.

It is further submitted that in relation to Crime No. 267/2020, the petitioner was granted regular bail by this Court vide order dated 06.09.2022 passed in M.Cr.C. No.35553/2022, subject to deposit of an amount of Rs.45,96,000/- within a period of 30 days.

The time for deposit was subsequently extended by this Court vide order dated 03.03.2025 passed in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10380 2 MCRC-57681-2025 M.Cr.C. No.9390/2025 and thereafter, one further opportunity was granted to the petitioner vide order dated 17.09.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.26402/2025.

It is further submitted that while granting bail to the petitioner in respect of the other crime numbers as well,
the Court extended the same relief subject to deposit of the defalcated amount in the respective cases.

3. It is further submitted that since petitioner was in jail and due to his judicial custody, the substantial amount involved in the respective cases, could not deposit the said amount within the stipulated period.

sentences.text: applications preferred by the petitioner under Section 70(2) of Cr.P.C. for cancellation of warrants were rejected in RCT No.7129/2020, RCT No.7128/2020 and RCT No.8066/2020.
It is further submitted that in compliance with the bail orders passed by the Court, the petitioner has since deposited the requisite amounts before the Trial Court at Bhopal (M.P.).
Accordingly, amount of Rs.45,96,000/- in FDR-1 and Rs.45,96,000/- in FDR-2 were deposited on 30.10.2025 and amount of Rs.14,76,500/- in FDR-3 was deposited on 17.11.2025.

Copies of the deposit receipts along with the relevant order sheets are collectively annexed as Annexure- A/8 with this petition and the certified copies of the Trial Court orders have also been placed on record.

It is, therefore, prayed that in view of the petitioner having duly complied with all the conditions imposed by the Court while granting bail, learned Trial Court may be directed to consider the petitioner's application under Section 72(2) of BNSS, 2023 for cancellation of the arrest warrants issued against him in RCT No.7129/2020, RCT No.7128/2020 and RCT No.8066/2020 in accordance with law.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the prayer on the ground that petitioner is having other cases of similar nature.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10380 3 MCRC-57681-2025 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.

6. In view of the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner, particularly submission regarding the condition to deposit the defalcated amount imposed while granting bail has now been duly complied with, this Court is of the opinion that learned Trial Court shall examine the petitioner's application for cancellation of the arrest warrants in light of such compliance.

7. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, learned Trial Court is directed to consider and pass an appropriate order on the petitioner's application under Section 72(2) of BNSS, 2023 for cancellation of the arrest warrants issued against petitioner in RCT No.7129/2020, RCT No.7128/2020 and RCT No.8066/2020 in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible.
8. With the aforesaid directions, the petition stands disposed of.
Let a copy of this order be transmitted to the Court concerned.
(B. P. SHARMA)
